### Historical audit: H0140

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/hint-codex-experiments/runs/codex_parallel_12/lanes/codex_parallel_12_lane1/codex_parallel_12_lane1_B_r2/infer_logs/igel-persist-feature-schema/turn_1/trajs.json`. Event references and character ranges below refer to this file’s supplied decoded observations.

| Aspect | Evidence and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Goal | The task name suggests persisting an Igel feature schema; the student’s search targeted schema, `description.json`, fit, evaluate, predict, export and dataset features. The full task specification is not visible, so exact requirements remain unknown (main agent events 3 and 5, characters [0,812) and [0,831)). |
| Autonomous exploration | The student inspected the repository, Git status, the `main` branch and instruction-file locations (events 1–2, [0,726) and [0,3432)). It then attempted to create `fix/persist-feature-schema` from `main`, chaining a source search after that command. Git returned `fatal: invalid reference: main`, so the chained search did not run (events 3–4, [0,812) and [0,345)). A subsequent command inspected branches, remotes and feature-related locations; it showed detached HEAD and `master` at `bf4544d`, and listed matching source locations (events 5–6, [0,831) and [0,4856)). |
| Changes and validation | The student reported no changes or commits and asked whether to branch from `master` instead (event 7, [0,787)). The supplied inventory records a zero-byte patch and formal result of 0/24 fail-to-pass and 2/2 pass-to-pass tests. No student-run tests or implementation are visible. This is an **empty patch, formally not solved**, not evidence of an implemented algorithm failing. |
| Teacher input | Shared hint files are listed as available, but their contents and the captured system prompt are not provided here. No delivered teacher event or adoption is visible; availability does not establish receipt or influence. |
| Termination | The session ended normally with the clarification request; the metadata records `end_turn` (top-level metadata, [0,4721)). The failed Git command was a concrete workflow blocker, not evidence of a technical interruption of the session. |

**Lessons and uncertainty.** A transferable observation is that a missing requested base can stop a chained implementation workflow even when another local branch points to the current commit; inspecting references makes that blocker explicit. The branch names, commit and schema search are specific to this task. It remains unknown whether branching from `master` was permitted, what the full feature-schema requirements or teacher guidance were, or whether any implementation would have passed. No scene is involved, so scene geometry, materials, pose and rendering checks do not apply.
